info.name: Handpoint Back-Office API
info.description:
Direct-to-gateway back-office operations compatible with **all** Handpoint integration paths (Android SDK, iOS SDK, PAX, Hilite, Cloud API).

None of these requests require a card reader or cardholder interaction — they go straight to the Handpoint gateway over HTTPS. Use them alongside any existing SDK integration to add reversal, remote charging, tip adjustment, batch management, and reporting capabilities.

**Environment:** set `env` to `com` (production) or `io` (staging). All base URLs resolve as `cloud.handpoint.{{env}}` or `txnfeed.handpoint.{{env}}`.

**GUID / originalGuid:** the transaction identifier returned by your SDK integration (Android: `transactionResult.EFTTransactionID`, iOS: `transactionResult.efttransactionID`, PAX/Cloud API: `efttransactionID` / `transactionID`). Set the `GUID` collection variable to use it across requests.

variable.description: AnalyticsApiKey — same value as api_key (ApiKeyCloud). Set once to use in Transaction Feed requests.
Terminal serial number — from List Devices
Transaction GUID from your SDK (efttransactionID / EFTTransactionID). Set this before using Reversal or reporting requests.
Card token from a saleAndTokenizeCard / tokenizeCard / GET /token operation. Required for Remote Sale.
Terminal model — from List Devices response (e.g. PAXA920)
UUID v4 — generated by the pre-request script on Remote Sale; also used by Search Transactions

item.name: Setup
item.description:
Verify credentials and retrieve the list of terminals assigned to the merchant account.

**`serial_number`** is used by Batch Close, Batch Summary, and Tip Adjustment. Copy it from the List Devices response and set the `serial_number` collection variable.

request.description:
Returns all PAX terminals assigned to this merchant API key.

Run this first to confirm your credentials and discover `serial_number` and `terminal_type` values to use in transaction requests — both fields are required in `POST /transactions` and must exactly match what this endpoint returns.

- HTTP 200 = valid key
- HTTP 403 = wrong or missing `ApiKeyCloud` header
- Terminal absent from list = error `1004` on transaction requests

item.name: Back-Office Operations
item.description:
All requests in this folder go directly to the Handpoint gateway — no terminal, no cardholder interaction, no polling. Each returns a synchronous HTTP 200/400 response.

**Amount units vary by endpoint:**
- Reversal: major units decimal string (`"10.00"`) — or omit for full reversal
- Remote Sale / Refund: major units decimal string (`"10.00"` = €10.00)
- Tip Adjustment: major units **number** (`5` = $5.00, no quotes)
- Pre-Auth Increase / Decrease / Capture: major units decimal string

**Success check:** HTTP 200 + `httpStatus: 200` + `issuerResponseCode: "00"` (or `statusMessage: "reversed"` for Reversal). No `finStatus`.

body.raw:
{
  "originalGuid": "{{GUID}}",         // guid from the original transaction (Poll Result / Get by GUID)
  "amount": "10.00",                   // MAJOR units decimal string | required for partial reversal only; omit for full reversal
  "currency": "{{currency}}"           // ISO 4217 | required for partial reversal only
  //,"messageReasonCode": "CUSTOMER_CANCELLATION"   // optional — default: CUSTOMER_CANCELLATION
  /*
  messageReasonCode allowed values:
  CUSTOMER_CANCELLATION, UNSPECIFIED_NO_ACTION_TAKEN, SUSPECTED_MALFUNCTION,
  FORMAT_ERROR_NO_ACTION_TAKEN, COMPLETED_PARTIALLY, ORIGINAL_AMOUNT_INCORRECT,
  RESPONSE_RECEIVED_TOO_LATE, CARD_ACCEPTOR_DEVICE_UNABLE_TO_COMPLETE_TRANSACTION,
  DEPOSIT_OUT_OF_BALANCE, NO_CHECK_IN_ENVELOPE, PAYMENT_OUT_OF_BALANCE,
  DEPOSIT_OUT_OF_BALANCE_APPLIED_CONTENTS, PAYMENT_OUT_OF_BALANCE_APPLIED_CONTENTS,
  UNABLE_TO_DELIVER_MESSAGE_TO_POINT_OF_SERVICE, SUSPECTED_MALFUNCTION_CARD_RETAINED,
  SUSPECTED_MALFUNCTION_CARD_RETURNED, SUSPECTED_MALFUNCTION_TRACK_3_NOT_UPDATED,
  SUSPECTED_MALFUNCTION_NO_CASH_DISPENSED, TIMED_OUT_AT_TAKING_MONEY_NO_CASH_DISPENSED,
  TIMED_OUT_AT_TAKING_CARD_CARD_RETAINED_AND_NO_CASH_DISPENSED,
  INVALID_RESPONSE_NO_ACTION_TAKEN, TIMEOUT_WAITING_FOR_RESPONSE,
  PREMATURE_CHIP_CARD_REMOVAL, CHIP_CARD_DECLINES_TRANSACTION, SIGNATURE_TIMEOUT,
  MERCHANT_REVERSAL_SIGNATURE_DECLINED, NO_REVERSAL_REASON_CODE
  */
}

request.description:
Reverses any transaction — sale, refund, or pre-authorization — synchronously, with no terminal or cardholder interaction required.

**`originalGuid`:** the `guid` (or `efttransactionID`) from the original transaction result. Retrieve it from the Poll Result, the Get by GUID endpoint, or the `GUID` collection variable set automatically by the Poll Result test script.

**Full reversal:** provide only `originalGuid`. The entire authorized amount is released.

**Partial reversal:** include `amount` (major units decimal string, e.g. `"10.00"`) and `currency` (ISO 4217). Only the specified amount is reversed; the remainder stays settled.

**`messageReasonCode`:** optional. Defaults to `CUSTOMER_CANCELLATION`. See body comments for the full list of allowed values.

**Success:** HTTP 200 + `httpStatus: 200`. No `finStatus` — this is a synchronous operation. Check `statusMessage: "reversed"` to confirm.

This endpoint replaces `/moto/reversal`, `saleReversal`, `refundReversal`, and `preAuthorizationReversal` for all no-reader reversal scenarios.

exec: // Back-office remote sale: no terminal required. Charges a stored cardToken directly.
// EPI only — EmerchantPay and Paystrax do not support back-office card-token remote sale.
// Back-office sale returns HTTP 200 synchronously (no polling).
// Success: check httpStatus === 200 (integer field in body).
// The reversal GUID is in the 'guid' field (NOT 'transactionID').
console.log('GUID for reversal set to:', body.guid);

request.description:
Charges a stored card token from your server — no terminal interaction, no cardholder present. EPI only.

**`amount`:** **major units** as a decimal string — `"10.00"` = €10.00. NOT minor units. Do NOT send `"1000"` expecting €10.00.

**`cardToken`:** obtained from a prior `saleAndTokenizeCard` or `GET /transactions/{id}/token`. Stored in the CARD_TOKEN collection variable.

**`transactionReference`:** UUID v4. Include for idempotency.

**Response:** HTTP 200 synchronous — no 202/polling. Check `httpStatus === 200` (integer field in body) for success. There is no `finStatus` field in this response.

**Reversal GUID:** the `guid` field in the response — NOT `transactionID`. Use in `POST /reversal` with `originalGuid`.

**Error `3107`:** Mandatory CVV is configured for this merchant's CNP — the token endpoint cannot supply CVV. Contact Handpoint to disable mandatory CVV.
**Error `5252`:** Token provider (ProCharge) is temporarily down — the token is valid, retry later.

**MOTO requirement:** Remote Sale uses the `/moto/sale` endpoint. **MOTO must be enabled for the merchant both in Handpoint and at the acquirer** before this endpoint will process successfully. Contact Handpoint support to enable MOTO.

**AVS (Address Verification System):** Include a `billing` object to pass cardholder billing address for AVS. AVS must be enabled on the merchant's acquirer agreement.

| Field | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `billing.zipCode` | Yes (within billing) | Cardholder billing ZIP / postal code |
| `billing.address` | No | Cardholder billing street address |

AVS result is returned in the response as `addressVerification.resultCode` (Android SDK 7.1015.0+, MoTo path only — not present in Cloud API poll responses).

**AVS result (Android SDK 7.1015.0+):** When a `billing` object is included and the acquirer performs AVS, the response contains an `addressVerification` object:

```json
"addressVerification": {
  "resultCode": "FULL_MATCH"
}
```

| `resultCode` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `FULL_MATCH` | Address + ZIP match |
| `EXACT_MATCH` | Exact 9-digit ZIP + address match |
| `ADDRESS_MATCH` | Address only matched |
| `ZIP_MATCH` | ZIP only matched |
| `ZIP9_MATCH` | 9-digit ZIP matched |
| `NO_MATCH` | Neither address nor ZIP matched |
| `UNSUPPORTED` | AVS not supported by acquirer |
| `INTERNATIONAL` | Non-US card (international) |
| `RETRY` | Retry requested |
| `UNAVAILABLE` | AVS unavailable |
| `UNKNOWN` | Unrecognized code |

> **Note:** `addressVerification` appears in Android SDK 7.1015.0+ for MoTo operations via the direct gateway path. It does **not** appear in Cloud API `GET /transaction-result` responses.

Processes a linked refund without requiring the card or terminal to be present. Refunds against an original transaction identified by its GUID.

**Amount:** major units as a decimal string — `"10.00"` = €10.00. Different from the minor units used by `POST /transactions`.

**`originalGuid`:** the `guid` / `efttransactionID` from the original sale result (set the `GUID` collection variable from Poll Result).

**MOTO requirement:** Remote Refund uses the `/moto/refund` endpoint. **MOTO must be enabled for the merchant both in Handpoint and at the acquirer** before this endpoint will process successfully. Contact Handpoint support to enable MOTO.

**Card-present alternative:** use **Refund — EMV Linked** (Card-Present) when the cardholder is present at the terminal.

**Success:** HTTP 200 + `httpStatus: 200` + `guid` present. Note: `issuerResponseCode` is not returned in the remote refund response body (check `issuerResponseText` instead). No `finStatus`.

Adds a tip to a completed sale before the batch closes. EPI merchants only.

**`GUID`:** the `transactionID` from the sale result (the GUID variable in this collection).

**`amount`:** tip in **major currency units** as a number — NOT minor units. `5` = $5.00, `5.25` = $5.25. Do NOT send `500` expecting $5.00.

**Constraints:**
- Must be called before the day's batch closes (~11 PM EST for most EPI merchants)
- Not available on HiLite paths or Cordova
- Not available on EmerchantPay or Paystrax (use `amount` in the original sale request for those acquirers)
- `transactionID` must come from a SALE — not a reversal or pre-auth

**On success:** HTTP 200, body `{"statusMessage": "tip adjusted"}`.
**On failure after batch close:** HTTP 400 with error specific to acquirer.

response.name: 400 — Batch already closed

request.description:
**Preferred tokenization method:** retrieving a token via this endpoint is safer than `saleAndTokenizeCard` because it decouples the transaction approval from the tokenization step. If the token provider is unavailable at the time of the sale, `saleAndTokenizeCard` will fail the entire operation. With this endpoint, the sale completes normally and the token can be retrieved later from any approved transaction — no card re-swipe required.

Retrieves a card token for a past `SALE` transaction without re-charging the cardholder. EPI only.

**`GUID`:** must be the `transactionID` of a SALE-type transaction (not a reversal, refund, or pre-auth). The test script in Poll Result sets this automatically.

**After a partial approval → cancel flow:** the polled `transactionID` is the reversal's ID, not the sale. Use `GET /transactions/{txnRef}/status/all` and pick the entry where `type == "SALE"` to find the correct GUID.

**Error `3112`:** `transactionID` is not a SALE (e.g. you used a reversal ID).
**Error `TOKENIZATION_NOT_ENABLED`:** tokenization is not configured for this merchant — contact Handpoint.

response.name: 400 — Transaction not eligible (error 3112)

item.name: Pre-Authorization (Back-Office)
item.description:
Back-office lifecycle steps for an existing pre-authorization hold.

**Pre-Authorization Create** is a card-present operation handled by your SDK integration (Android SDK, iOS SDK, PAX, or Cloud API). Once the hold is placed, use these endpoints to adjust, capture, or reverse it — no terminal required.

**`originalTransactionId`:** the `efttransactionID` / `EFTTransactionID` from the Pre-Auth Create result. Set this as your `GUID` collection variable.

**Supported acquirers:** EPI, EmerchantPay, Paystrax.

request.description:
Adjust (increase or decrease) a pre-authorization hold amount before capture.
**Synchronous back-office operation — no terminal required.** Returns HTTP 200 directly.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `originalGuid` | `transactionID` from the Pre-Authorization Create result |
| `increaseAmount` | Amount to adjust the hold by, in **major units** — e.g. `"5.00"` = $5.00 |
| `tipAmount` | Tip component of the adjustment — typically `"0"` |
| `subtract` | `"1"` to decrease the hold; increase by setting `increaseAmount` positively |

**Error 3211:** Pre-auth already captured, voided, or not found.

response.name: 400 — Error 3211 (already captured/voided)

request.description:
Capture a previously authorised pre-authorization hold. **Synchronous back-office operation — no terminal required.** Returns HTTP 200 directly.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `originalGuid` | `transactionID` from the Pre-Authorization Create result |
| `capturedAmount` | Final capture amount in **major units** — e.g. `"45.00"` = $45.00. Must be ≤ the pre-auth hold amount. |

response.name: 400 — Error 3211 (already captured/voided)

request.description:
Triggers end-of-day settlement for EPI merchants. **Must be called once per business day.** Missing a batch close causes ERR 005 (batch number mismatch) on all subsequent transactions.

**EPI only** — do NOT call for EmerchantPay or Paystrax merchants (they settle automatically).

**`batchNumber` is optional** (implemented in GW-350). The gateway automatically resolves the last open batch number for the terminal from its internal store. Include `batchNumber` only when you need to target a specific batch.

**Minimum required body:** `serialNumber` + `deviceType` — that's it.

**Field naming:** `deviceType` and `serialNumber` (camelCase) — NOT `terminal_type` / `serial_number` (the snake_case names used by `POST /transactions`). Different naming convention on batch endpoints.

**Timing:** call after the last transaction of the business day. Typical EPI auto-close is ~11 PM EST.

**Error cases:**

| Scenario | Response |
|---|---|
| `deviceType` doesn't match the serial number | 400 with `errorCode: 5001` (NullPointerException from Viscus) |
| `serialNumber` not found for this merchant | 500 Internal Server Error |
| Terminal has never transacted (no batch in store) | Error similar to wrong batch number |

**Response note:** The `transactionCount` and `netAmount` fields appear on staging (dummy acquirer) but are **not returned by TSYS** in production. Do not rely on them. Use `batchStatus: "CLOSED"` and `issuerResponseCode: "00"` as success indicators. TSYS production responses include `customFields.entry.key: "issuerBatchCloseLocalTimestamp"` with the local close time.

Returns a summary of the current batch for a terminal. EPI only. Same field naming as Batch Close (`deviceType` / `serialNumber`).

**`batchNumber` is optional** — gateway auto-resolves the last batch for the terminal. Include only when targeting a specific historical batch.

**Note:** `transactionCount` and `netAmount` are returned by the staging dummy acquirer but may not be present in all production acquirer responses. Check `batchStatus` and `issuerResponseCode` for success.

item.name: Transaction Feed (Reporting)
item.description:
Query the Handpoint Transaction Feed to retrieve and search transaction history.

**`AnalyticsApiKey` header:** same value as your `ApiKeyCloud` API key — set the `analytics_key` collection variable to your API key. Do NOT leave it as `{{api_key}}` — the Transaction Feed requires the `AnalyticsApiKey` header, not `ApiKeyCloud`.

**Response format:** Transaction Feed fields differ from Cloud API poll results (e.g. `guid` not `transactionID`, `currCode` not `currency`, `type: "Sale"` not `"SALE"`). See the Get Transaction by GUID request for the field mapping.

**`GUID`:** set the collection variable to look up a specific transaction by its gateway identifier.

request.description:
Retrieves a single transaction record from the Transaction Feed by its `guid` (the GUID variable).

**Note:** The Transaction Feed uses different field names than the Cloud API poll result:

| Transaction Feed field | Cloud API poll result equivalent |
|---|---|
| `guid` | `transactionID` |
| `transactionReference` | `transactionReference` (same) |
| `currCode` | `currency` |
| `type` | `type` (different values: `"Sale"` vs `"SALE"`) |
| `paymentScenario` | `paymentScenario` (same) |
| `maskedCardNumber` | `maskedCardNumber` (different mask format — BIN shown here) |

**`AnalyticsApiKey`** — same value as `ApiKeyCloud`; set the `analytics_key` collection variable to your API key.

Useful for UNDEFINED recovery when you have the `guid` and need to confirm settlement status via the feed.

request.description:
Searches the transaction feed by time range and optional filters. Primary use case: UNDEFINED recovery when `transactionReference` recovery is unavailable.

**`AnalyticsApiKey`** — same value as `ApiKeyCloud`; set the `analytics_key` collection variable.

**`startDate` / `endDate`:** format `yyyyMMddHHmmss` (e.g. `"20260905120000"`).

**`time_zone`:** IANA timezone string (e.g. `"Europe/London"`, `"America/New_York"`, `"UTC"`).

**`dummy`:** controls inclusion of test/simulator transactions:
- `"INCLUDE"` — include both real and dummy transactions
- `"ONLY"` — only dummy/simulator transactions
- `"NO"` — only real transactions

**Available `filters` fields:** `transactionReference`, `amount`, `maskedCardNumber`, `cardTypeId`, `approvalCode`, `terminalSerialNumber`

**UNDEFINED recovery pattern:** filter by `terminalSerialNumber` + narrow time window (±5 min around the original request). Match by `transactionReference` to identify the specific transaction — do NOT match by amount alone (multiple transactions may share the same amount).
